fault_line: Lone-wolf terror or a warning sign? Ministers call it far-right terror before the motive is proven -- premature label or honest warning?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- ministers' own statements, AP/Reuters] Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said at a Krakow press conference that the 25-year-old Polish gunman held 'very, very radical views' and that 'everything indicates that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies' -- explicitly preliminary: the minister stressed this 'will have to be verified'. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz called the shooting an 'act of terror' -- a characterisation, NOT a charge: no terrorism charge has been announced and prosecutors have not formally classified the case. [VERIFIED FACT -- AP/Reuters] One of the six killed was a British citizen; five of the wounded were foreign nationals. The suspect is 25 (AP: officials corrected the earlier figure of 24); a Polish citizen who acted alone; shot and wounded by police, in critical condition after a second operation; drove into Main Market Square firing an AR-15-type rifle from his car (he held a firearms licence); numerous firearms found in his car; three family members (two women, one man) found dead at his home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, ~150km NE of Krakow. Krakow mourning until Nov 11; President Nawrocki began the process for national mourning Nov 8-9. [UNVERIFIED] Motive: no official has said why he chose the square or targeted anyone; suspect not named; no charges announced; whether the firearms were legally owned is under investigation.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct publisher families with declared tiers: AP (T1) and Reuters (T1). CNN, CBS, nacionale, britbrief, Glasgow Times and fish4news have NO declared tier in the registry -- reported with attribution only, they do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: Casualty counts conflicted through the day (5 then 6 killed; 15 vs 16 wounded incl. suspect + 2 officers); suspect age reported as both 24 and 25 (AP: officials corrected 24 to 25). Defence minister denied reports the suspect was a serving/former soldier. No evidence supporting the far-right assessment has been reported; the minister himself said it needs verification. No official has established a motive, and no terrorism charge exists -- the 'act of terror' label is ministerial rhetoric, not a legal finding.
